name: Qualify and onboard new drivers
summary: Each candidate from recruiting, and each driver an owner-operator puts on the road, is road-tested by a driver trainer, has a driver qualification file built and checked by a compliance specialist, is set up in payroll, the ELD and dispatch systems, and attends two to three days of orientation. Newly licensed drivers then spend three to six weeks with a mentor driver before a final road test by a second trainer. The process is slow because trainers and training tractors are shared across 38 terminals, documents such as medical certificates arrive late, and the finishing program ties up a mentor and a tractor for weeks.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian LTL and truckload carrier of about 3,000 employees with 18 driver trainers, 10 training tractors and a compliance team in its safety department.
baseline.notes: About 53 new drivers a month: about 45 company hires and about 8 drivers employed by owner-operators. About 30% need the finishing program, 20% get a check ride, 30% run into the US and need a US medical certificate.

trigger: Recruiting hands over a candidate who accepted a conditional offer, or owner-operator contracting submits a driver the owner-operator wants to put on the road.
end_state: The driver is qualified on file and available for dispatch, or the candidate failed the road test or was released during finishing.

volume.seasonality: Larger classes in January to April and August to September; fewer starts in December.

evidence.note: Organisation process map volume, from about 500 company hires a year (US turnover benchmarks scaled down) plus owner-operators' drivers.

surge.cause: Pre-peak hiring classes and spring driving-school graduations

evidence.note: Follows the recruiting surge with a one to three week lag; author's estimate.

roles.title: Compliance specialist (hours of service and driver files)

evidence.note: Qualification file build, system set-up and sign-off for about 55 drivers a month; the rest of the 12-person team audits logs and renewals. Author's estimate.
Road tests, orientation, check rides and finishing evaluations; the other trainers run refresher, winter and coaching courses. Author's estimate.
Employee set-up for about 45 company drivers a month. Author's estimate.
Tractor assignment and release to dispatch; terminal supervisors do the same for LTL hires. Not listed for this process in the org file. Author's estimate.

New drivers in orientation and finishing, and the mentor drivers who ride with them: about 16 trainees a month for about five weeks keeps about 18 trainee-mentor pairs on the road at any time, plus orientation days. Stands in for new hires of every division. Not listed for this process in the org file. Author's estimate.

systems.name: Safety management system (driver files, collisions, roadside inspections)
Email, phone system and contact centre software
Electronic logging devices and telematics platform
Transportation management system (LTL and truckload operations, billing, rating)
Learning management system and training records

steps.name: Open driver qualification file
steps.description: The compliance specialist receives the candidate handoff from recruiting, opens a driver qualification file in the safety system and checks that the application, abstract, verifications and consents arrived with it. Missing items are listed for follow-up later in the file build.

error.defect_description: A missing document not noticed at intake.

evidence.note: Qualification file contents follow 49 CFR 391.51 for cross-border drivers; Canadian facility audits ask for the same driver file records.

steps.name: Schedule road test and book training tractor
steps.description: A driver trainer looks at the trainer calendar and the training tractor bookings, picks a slot at the candidate's nearest terminal (recruiting has usually pencilled one in with the offer), and confirms the date and time with the candidate by phone and email.

next.condition: candidate is at a terminal without a resident trainer

evidence.note: Ten training tractors and eighteen trainers serve 38 terminals (organisation file); share needing travel is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Trainer drives to the candidate's terminal
steps.description: The trainer drives the training tractor or a company car from the home terminal to the candidate's terminal, often combining two or three road tests and an orientation in one trip. Storms and closed highways postpone the trip.

evidence.note: Distances between Ontario, Quebec and western terminals; author's estimate.

steps.name: Conduct road test
steps.description: The trainer watches the candidate do a full pre-trip inspection, couple and uncouple a trailer, drive in city traffic and on the highway, turn, brake, back into a dock and park, scoring each item on the road test form. The trainer decides pass, retest after coaching, or fail.

control.basis: 49 CFR 391.31 road test (or accepted equivalent) for drivers operating into the US; insurer requirement for domestic drivers

evidence.note: Minimum road test content and certificate.

steps.name: Complete road test certificate
steps.description: The trainer signs the road test form, completes the road test certificate with the tractor and trailer types and distance driven, gives the driver a copy and uploads the originals to the driver's file in the safety system.

error.defect_description: Certificate missing vehicle type or signature.

evidence.note: Certificate content and filing.

steps.name: Verify documents and build qualification file
steps.description: The compliance specialist checks the licence class and expiry, medical certificate dates, abstract date, previous-employer responses, TDG and border documents against a checklist, and records expiry dates in the safety system so renewals are flagged. Cross-border drivers without a current US medical certificate are sent for one.

error.defect_description: An expiry date keyed wrongly, so a renewal is missed later.

control.basis: 49 CFR 391.51 driver qualification file; provincial National Safety Code driver record requirements checked in facility audits

next.condition: cross-border driver needs a US medical examination
owner-operator's driver, not a company employee

evidence.note: Driver qualification file contents and retention.

steps.name: Chase missing documents
steps.description: The compliance specialist emails and phones the driver, or the recruiter, for the missing licence copy, medical certificate, signed consent or employer response, and logs each request in the file.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Driver obtains US medical examination
steps.description: The driver books and attends a medical examination with a certified medical examiner and returns the medical examiner's certificate, which the compliance specialist later files.

evidence.note: Medical examiner's certificate is part of the US qualification file; clinic waits are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Create employee and payroll record
steps.description: The HR coordinator enters the new driver in the HR and payroll system with pay rate, pay basis (mileage, hourly or trip), banking, tax forms, benefits waiting period and, at unionised terminals, union membership and seniority date.

error.defect_description: Wrong pay rate or pay basis keyed.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Set up ELD, fuel card and dispatch profiles
steps.description: The compliance specialist creates the driver's ELD login and HOS cycle settings, requests a fuel card, and re-types the driver into the transportation management system so dispatch can assign loads, because none of these systems share a driver master.

error.defect_description: ELD cycle or home terminal set wrongly.

evidence.note: Separate ELD, fuel card and TMS driver records were common in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: New driver attends orientation
steps.description: The new driver spends two to three paid days in the orientation class: company policies, hours of service and the ELD, trip inspections, cargo securement, TDG, customs and border procedures for cross-border drivers, collision reporting and the drug and alcohol policy. The driver signs the policy acknowledgements.

evidence.note: Carriers add their own training on top of entry-level licence training; class length is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Trainer delivers orientation
steps.description: A driver trainer runs the classroom and yard sessions for a class of about six new drivers, demonstrates the ELD and inspection routine, and marks attendance and quiz results. The figure here is one driver's share of the trainer's time.

evidence.note: Class of about six; author's estimate.

steps.name: Issue TDG certificate and record training
steps.description: The trainer issues the employer's TDG training certificate, enters the orientation modules, quiz scores and certificate expiry in the learning management system, and files copies in the driver file.

control.basis: Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations Part 6: training certificate before handling or transporting dangerous goods

evidence.note: Employer-issued TDG certificates with 36-month expiry (organisation file); author's estimate of time.

steps.name: Assign tractor and introduce dispatch
steps.description: The driver manager or terminal supervisor assigns a tractor, issues keys, fuel card and permits, walks the driver through dispatch, trip pay and messaging, and decides from the file and road test whether the driver needs the finishing program or a check ride.

next.condition: newly licensed or under one year of experience

evidence.note: Carriers hiring newly licensed drivers must run finishing or mentoring programs for insurance; shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Run finishing program with a mentor driver
steps.description: The new driver runs revenue loads with a mentor driver for three to six weeks, first watching, then driving most of the miles with the mentor beside them, then driving their own truck while the mentor follows. Both are paid; the hours shown are working hours for each of the two (about 50 to 60 a week), and the off-duty days in between appear as the wait before the final road test.

control.basis: Insurer requirement for a documented finishing or mentoring program before newly licensed drivers run solo

evidence.note: Finishing programs of three to six weeks or more with an instructor or mentor at Ontario and Alberta carriers.

steps.name: Trainer evaluates trainee weekly
steps.description: A driver trainer meets the trainee and mentor each week, rides along for part of a shift, reviews ELD logs and any telematics events, and records progress and the skills still to practise.

evidence.note: Weekly evaluations described for a carrier finishing program.

steps.name: Final road test by a second trainer
steps.description: At the end of the scheduled program weeks (the wait here is the off-duty and home time inside the program that the hours above leave out), a different trainer from the one who coached the trainee gives a final road test in the trainee's assigned truck and decides whether the trainee runs solo, needs more weeks with the mentor, or is let go.

control.basis: Insurer-approved finishing program: independent final evaluation

evidence.note: Final road test by a different instructor.

steps.name: Check ride with experienced driver
steps.description: A driver trainer rides with an experienced new hire on a first local run to watch inspections, coupling, backing and log use in company equipment, and notes anything to correct before the driver goes solo.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Sign off qualification file before first dispatch
steps.description: The compliance specialist rechecks the file against the checklist (application, abstract, road test certificate, medical, training, consents) and marks the driver as qualified in the safety system. Previous-employer responses still outstanding go on a 30-day follow-up list.

control.basis: 49 CFR 391.51 and 391.23(c); National Safety Code driver records

evidence.note: Previous-employer investigation must be in the file within 30 days of employment.

steps.name: Release driver to dispatch
steps.description: The driver manager or terminal supervisor marks the driver available in the transportation management system with home terminal, fleet and cross-border status, so planners can assign the first solo load.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Close candidate or end employment
steps.description: When a candidate fails the road test or a trainee is released, the compliance specialist records the reason, notifies the recruiter and HR, closes the file and keeps it for the retention period.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Road test retest
exceptions.description: The candidate makes correctable errors (backing, coupling) and is coached and retested a few days later.

exceptions.name: Finishing extended
exceptions.description: The final road test shows gaps and the trainee spends one to three more weeks with the mentor.

exceptions.name: Medical certificate delay
exceptions.description: A cross-border driver waits more than a week for a medical examination appointment and starts on domestic runs or waits.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from candidate handoff to release for first solo dispatch
benchmarks.population: New company and owner-operator drivers at a mid-size Canadian carrier, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Experienced drivers: road test, file build and orientation in one to two weeks (author's estimate); newly licensed drivers add finishing programs of three to six weeks or more.

benchmarks.population: Ontario MELT (from July 2017) and the national standard approved in 2020; Alberta 113, Manitoba and Saskatchewan 121.5

evidence.note: Licence training before a candidate applies; carriers add orientation and finishing.

pain_points.description: Eighteen trainers and ten training tractors cover 38 terminals, so road tests wait for a slot and trainers spend hours driving between terminals.

evidence.note: Counts from the organisation file; waits are the author's estimate.

pain_points.description: The same driver is typed into the safety system, HR and payroll, the ELD platform, the fuel card portal and the TMS.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Finishing programs tie up a mentor driver and a tractor for three to six weeks per newly licensed driver, yet insurers require them before such drivers run solo.

evidence.note: Insurance-driven finishing and mentoring requirements.

pain_points.description: Medical certificates, consents and previous-employer responses arrive late and gaps in the file are a facility audit finding.

evidence.note: Auditors request driver file records.

sources.title: 49 CFR 391.51 General requirements for driver qualification files
sources.publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
sources.supports: Driver qualification file holds the application, driving records, road test certificate, annual review, medical examiner's certificate and related documents; kept for the period of employment and three years after.

sources.title: 49 CFR 391.31 Road test
sources.publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
sources.supports: Road test given by the carrier or its designee in the type of vehicle the driver will be assigned, covering at least the pre-trip inspection, coupling and uncoupling, placing the vehicle in operation, use of controls and emergency equipment, driving in traffic and passing, turning, braking, backing and parking; examiner rates the test on a form and issues a certificate kept in the qualification file.

sources.title: 49 CFR 391.23 Investigation and inquiries
sources.publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
sources.supports: Within 30 days of employment beginning, obtain the driving record from every licensing authority of the past 3 years and investigate the driver's safety performance history with DOT-regulated employers of the past 3 years, including drug and alcohol violations, with the driver's written consent; previous employers must respond within 30 days; document good-faith efforts when they do not.

sources.title: Facility audits and new carrier compliance reviews
sources.supports: Facility auditors request driver file records and hours-of-service records with documentation that supports the reported hours, such as payroll records, gate tickets and fuel receipts; results can change the safety rating, add conditions or bring administrative penalties.

sources.title: Carriers reap rewards from their driving schools, finishing programs
sources.supports: Ontario and Alberta carriers' finishing programs for newly licensed drivers: Challenger three weeks in the yard, two weeks city and two weeks highway with an instructor; Kriska minimum six weeks starting with four days of classroom, weekly evaluations and a final road test by a different instructor; New Way three months; Musket several weeks with a mentor, driving own truck in week four.

sources.title: New drivers traverse difficult road to employment
sources.supports: Most carriers require at least one year's experience, mainly because of insurance; carriers with fleet policies can hire newly licensed drivers if they run onboarding, finishing or mentoring programs; carriers prefer Canadian experience for cross-border work; US visa waits delay new drivers' cross-border eligibility.

sources.title: Canada's truck drivers to require 103.5 hours of training
sources.supports: National entry-level training standard of 103.5 hours for Class 1/A (36.5 classroom, 17 yard, 50 behind the wheel) approved February 2020; Ontario MELT in force since July 2017; Manitoba and Saskatchewan 121.5 hours, Alberta 113 hours; CTA says many carriers still require recruits to take additional training.

sources.title: Turnover Remained Unchanged at Large Truckload Fleets in Fourth Quarter
sources.supports: US annualized driver turnover in 2020: large truckload fleets 90% (92% in Q4), small truckload 69%, LTL 13% (12% in Q4).

assumptions: The role tl-driver-longhaul stands in for the new hire and the mentor driver in every division; LTL pickup and delivery and linehaul hires follow the same steps at slightly different pay.

Finishing program hours count both mentor and trainee working time (people = 2) although they haul revenue loads at the same time, so labour cost per case overstates the incremental cost of finishing.
Training tractor use is one tractor for each road test plus travel; the finishing program uses a regular truckload tractor.

US rules (49 CFR 391) apply to drivers who will run into the US (about 30%); domestic drivers' files follow National Safety Code driver record rules, which could not be opened and are described from general knowledge.
Driver trainers work office hours; road tests postponed by storms are shown as a weather wait on trainer travel.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (wage x 1.30 for hourly staff, x 1.35 for salaried staff).

The staffing check counts 130 productive hours a month per FTE; drivers in finishing work 200 or more hours a month, so the implied FTE overstates driver headcount. About 47 FTE stated (40 of them drivers in orientation and finishing) is consistent with about 18 trainee-mentor pairs on the road at any time.
Simulated median cycle time sits a little above the 12-day benchmark because orientation runs weekly and road tests, medical certificates and HR set-up queue one after another for experienced hires.
